topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, outlines the lecture series, and presents the key learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Cancer etiology, intrinsic mutation risk, and epidemiological evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational drivers of cancer by examining the balance between intrinsic replication errors, inherited predisposition, and environmental exposures alongside global epidemiological data.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the oncogenic mechanisms of infectious agents and illustrate them in detail through the etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how physical and chemical agents induce DNA damage through direct adduct formation, oxidative stress, and host xenobiotic metabolic processing.

topics.label: Tumor promotion and the two-stage model of carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how non-mutagenic promoter substances stimulate signaling pathways and chronic inflammation to drive the clonal outgrowth of initiated cells.

topics.label: Host susceptibility factors and summary of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze how developmental timing and physiological states modify cancer vulnerability and synthesize the discussed mechanisms of carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Methods for identifying carcinogens and evaluating human risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review analytical, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to determine carcinogenicity and assess human exposure risks.

topics.label: Conclusion and closing remarks
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer delivers concluding remarks summarizing the core lecture themes and completes the presentation.
